name: Salt Flat Venom
summary: At the Mirage Raceway, Fizzle Brassbolts seeks hotter fuel for his rocket car. He believes scorpid venom from the Shimmering Flats can give it the fierce burn he needs.

sections.title: A Volatile Recipe
sections.body: At the Mirage Raceway, gnomish precision meets goblin audacity in contests of speed and invention. Fizzle Brassbolts wants more from fuel and clockwork parts. He seeks a mixture that burns hotter than common propellants and sends rocket cars racing across the dry salt lake at blistering speed.

sections.title: Saline Venom of the Salt Flats
sections.body: Scorpids in the Shimmering Flats may hold the key to Fizzle's new fuel. They endure an arid wasteland crusted with salt, and their venom carries an unusual amount of it. Fizzle sees a useful chemical payload in their deadly sting. He believes boiling and refining the venom, then treating it with exotic catalysts, can create the fierce combustion needed to leave the goblin pit crews behind.

faq.q: Why does Fizzle Brassbolts want scorpid venom?
faq.answer: Fizzle Brassbolts wants scorpid venom for rocket car fuel that burns extremely hot. He believes the unusual salt content in Shimmering Flats scorpids' venom is vital to his explosive mixture.

faq.q: Where can the necessary scorpids be found?
faq.answer: Scorpids roam the open Shimmering Flats, especially the western flats and desert sands away from the central racetrack.

faq.q: What will Fizzle do with the venom once collected?
aliases: how is venom turned to fuel
faq.answer: Fizzle plans to boil down the venom, treat it with a skipper-otomer, and mix it with a nega-catalyst for rocket propellant. He has misplaced his notes.

faq.q: Can members of both the Alliance and Horde help Fizzle?
faq.answer: Yes. Gnomes and goblins manage the Mirage Raceway under a neutral truce, so adventurers from either faction can help the pit crews without political interference.

faq.q: Why are gnomes and goblins racing in Thousand Needles?
faq.answer: The Shimmering Flats offer a vast, flat stretch of hard-packed salt without obstructions. That makes them a proving ground for experimental, high-speed rocket cars and dragsters.

faq.q: Does the fuel actually make the car fly?
faq.answer: Fizzle eagerly says the car will “fly,” but gnomish rocket vehicles on the salt flats are built to skim the ground at breakneck speed. Catastrophic liftoffs and crashes remain possible.

angles.text: As a gnome, you may recognize Fizzle's familiar ambition: relentless tinkering, risky chemistry, misplaced notes, and the urge to outshine goblin mechanics.
As an engineer, you can see how organic toxins and catalysts like skipper-otomers fuel the creative, volatile experiments of competitive vehicle craft.
